blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Bear Creek / Green Timbers: streets and boundaries

items.t: This neighbourhood is named for two parks: Bear Creek Park at 13750 88 Avenue and Green Timbers Urban Forest Park in the 14600 block of 100 Avenue.
The City places both parks in Whalley and City Centre, so the park names are older than the board sub-area name used for the housing around them.
Fraser Highway cuts the south side, where the future Green Timbers Station will sit at 140 Street and Fraser Highway, on the westernmost edge of Green Timbers Urban Forest.

blocks.text: Bear Creek / Green Timbers: the housing stock

items.t: Housing here wraps around protected parkland, rather than sitting inside a single plan area.

Schools confirmed by name and address in and around this area include Bear Creek Elementary at 13780 80 Avenue, Green Timbers Elementary at 8824 144 Street and Enver Creek Secondary at 14505 84 Avenue.
Green Timbers itself is second-growth forest: the land was completely logged by 1929, replanted as British Columbia's first reforestation project, and became a park in 1974.

blocks.text: Bear Creek / Green Timbers: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The local rule is park protection: Surrey residents voted in 1988 and 1996 to designate part of Green Timbers as an urban forest, a protected natural legacy, so the forest is not development land.
Lots backing onto Bear Creek or the Green Timbers forest need a riparian and tree check for the specific lot; the park pages do not state a setback for a private lot.

blocks.text: Bear Creek / Green Timbers: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: A glacial erratic, a large rock carried by glacial ice, sits on the trails in the northwestern part of Green Timbers park.
The Surrey Nature Centre sits inside Green Timbers, beside an arboretum of over 75 species and the 1930 Inaugural Plantation.
Bear Creek Park hosts the Surrey Arts Centre nearby, which the City names in its Whalley community description.

blocks.text: Bear Creek / Green Timbers: development and new projects

items.t: Full entry for this cluster: the Surrey–Langley SkyTrain is a 16-kilometre Expo Line extension along Fraser Highway from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, and Green Timbers is its first station east of King George.
Full entry for this cluster: a new destination athletics centre, the Bear Creek Park Stadium, is listed by the City among Newton's upcoming capital projects at Bear Creek Park.

blocks.text: Bear Creek / Green Timbers: getting around

items.t: Fraser Highway is the transit spine: the Surrey–Langley SkyTrain will run on it, with Green Timbers Station at 140 Street.
King George Station, west of Green Timbers, is the current Expo Line end and the start of the extension.

blocks.text: Bear Creek / Green Timbers: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check Bear Creek corridor lots against City riparian requirements; Bear Creek flows through British Manor Park and Bear Creek Park as a natural-area watercourse.

Check trees before planning any removal: the City states many of Surrey's more than 200 heritage-status trees are found in Green Timbers Park, and private-lot tree rules are a separate City check from park protection.

faq.a: One board sub-area with a compound name. In the SnapStats data it is a single sub-area of the Surrey community, and its listings all carry the single label "Bear Creek Green Timbers"; the name joins the Bear Creek Park ground (which the City places in Whalley, beside the Surrey Arts Centre) with the Green Timbers Urban Forest ground (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).
faq.q: Is Bear Creek Green Timbers one neighbourhood or two?

faq.a: One secondary suite per dwelling unit (habitable floor area at most 40% of the principal dwelling unit, never inside a coach house or garden suite), a coach house or garden suite of 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR, with lane access required for a coach house on smaller lots), and 3–4 SSMUH units on most lots by size band, up to 6 near a frequent bus stop.
